findings.summary: The instruction to make the directory argument absolute ('created if missing, then `cd` there and `pwd -P`', right after reading it) does not say to do it in a subshell. In every script `dir=` comes before `here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P)`. A top-level `cd "$dir"` there breaks `here`, and so `top`, whenever the script is started by a relative path. That is the form the README and acceptance items 1 and 2 use (`tools/copilot-acceptance/work.sh <model>`). Task 5's gate runs one `go -C` call from outside the module, so it would not catch this; only the operator's acceptance would.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/run.sh:22-24 (dir, then here, then top); hook.sh:19-20; work.sh, verify.sh, plan.sh, gatereview.sh, second.sh: dir= on the line before here=. Acceptance step 1 runs `tools/copilot-acceptance/work.sh <copilot model>`, where $0 is relative.
findings.fix: Pin the form: `dir=$(mkdir -p "$dir" && cd "$dir" && pwd -P) || die …` (the same for `work` in bypass.sh). That leaves the working directory unchanged. Optionally, have task 5's gate start one script by a relative path.

findings.section: Behaviour contract / P2; Decided here (how a report is compared)
findings.summary: 'The session table, from its heading line through the blank line after it' can be read as the report's `## …` Markdown heading, not the table's header row. Under that reading the title and the '`vloop run` exit N.' line are dropped too. The test and the program use the same phrase, so a session that reads it this way on both sides passes its own golden comparison and still loses the title.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/report.py:46-48: each report opens with `## …`, a blank line, '`vloop run` exit {rc}.', a blank line, and then the table header `| record | …` (gate-review's is `| round | record | …`, line 205).
findings.fix: Say 'from the table's header row (`| record | …`, or `| round | record | …` for gate-review) through the blank line after it; the `##` heading and the exit line before it stay'.

decisions: The per-session view is `--by session` on vloop metrics; a separate `vloop sessions` command was rejected. Sound: it reads the same records.

by_session is an optional property of metrics/v4, not a v5. It is emitted on every --json document, so close snapshots written from B37 on carry it, denial text included. Sound, but the snapshots grow.
`--by session` with --workspace is refused (exit 2), and export leaves by_session out.
Brief-review sessions stay out of the rows, as they stay out of metrics.
The kit becomes one Go program run with `go -C "$top" run`, not a vloop subcommand; jq was rejected. Sound: the probes spend credits.

The Go port reproduces the Python byte for byte, checked against goldens the Python generates, including emulating json.dumps and repr. This costs a lot to build for an acceptance tool. It is the only way to prove 'unchanged' without restating every table.

The reports' own session tables are replaced by the P1 view. This loses gate-review's per-folder round numbering, the per-record session/v3 'ok' column (now a count plus the invalid records) and the raw permission_denials JSON (now 'tool: text' lines).
The run report now validates each record against its own schema field, where it validated every record as session/v3.
Formatting choices: `#` has three digits; credits print '-' when absent and '0.00' when zero; a second-review row's phase is 'second-review'.
The goldens are regenerated from the base's Python in task 2's gate, so the gate needs python3 on the gate host while no go test does.
perl stays a dependency of bypass.sh.
checked: facts (runs.go folder order, phases and fields; metrics phase switch and denial sum; the --by refusals and messages in internal/cli/metrics.go; minSec rounding; the export deletion of by_task; metrics.v4 schema has no additionalProperties; B36's 13 records, first/last row values, total 5.670251600000001 and 8 denials against `vloop metrics --json`; the denial entry shapes in every record in this repo; report.py's six kinds and table layouts; hook.py VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE; bypass.sh's calls and perl; the .pyc in B24's T5 review; go.mod 1.27.1 for go -C; agent-eval precedent), consistency, rules (CLAUDE.md, repo architect constraints), runnability (task order against the single go check, help-text regeneration of docs/guide/commands.md, no existing test pins 'want task', task 2's gate surviving task 5)
